spec.seam: run_rebalday gained raw= so both arms burn off one load
spec.join: _rebalday_arm_cells keeps calendar / returns / spread cells in separate namespaces and _rebalday_cell_role names each moved cell, so the split is the published reading
spec.control: the same arm joined against itself; every cell must read delta 0.0 or the join machinery moved the numbers

cutoff_control.comparison: old raw arm vs today raw arm (arm held fixed)

answers.delta_units: each delta is in the units of its column: bp for spreads, percent per year for annualised returns, turns/yr for turnover, sessions for offsets -- the summary max is a max over mixed units and is a screen, not a quantity
answers.shift_verdict: the repair moves the returns while the trade calendar is untouched: the calendars disagree by the same schedule, what moved is the level
answers.reading: the repair reaches the calendar face: 33 of 114 cells move (0 calendar, 17 returns, 16 spread, 0 other) and 0 cell(s) exist on one arm only

honest: descriptive census only: no gate, no verdict on the strategy, no prereg, no trial count, no ledger booking

the split is a classification of moved cells, not a decomposition: a calendar cell and a return cell can move for one and the same repair, and the counts say how many cells each role lost, not how much of a change each role caused
spread_all_positive is published per arm as a verdict and is NOT joined: subtracting two booleans would book a delta with no units
the screened arm repairs prints inside the panel it is handed; it does not add or remove bars, so an unchanged universe_members count is a property of the repair, not evidence the panel is clean
the cutoff control joins an older raw face whose start set may be narrower, so its one-sided count is structural and only the shared cells carry the refresh reading
E97 counts the published numbers of this runner; the join covers the book/calendar/spread/answers/window cells, not the pointer fields
